question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says "When a door refuses to write a red's ticket, run_proof catches RedTicketRefused, raises an unticketed trouble, and re-raises the exception so the run exits without writing a ticket for that red. The red stays new for the next run to retry.", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline states: "Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it." When the ticket's work is built, some runs (those where a door refuses) will NOT write a ticket for a new red they found. The outline's exception clause ("unless one is already open") does not cover door refusal—a gate refusing is a new situation the outline did not anticipate. This violates the stated requirement that each run writes a ticket.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands; same reading as open-821fcdbe84f0 and open-67977da252c0. The ticket adds no run that skips the write. Every run calls the door for every new red (cairn/devices/tester/device.py:1007). A refusal is a door defect that exists today with nothing on disk; this ticket makes it fail the run, name the lacks in a trouble, and retry on every later run until the ticket lands.
